concerns.text: Only 20 non‑overlapping windows per interval length (total 60 windows) are sampled. Given the high variability of autocorrelation statistics, this sample size provides limited power to detect small deviations from zero, especially after Benjamini‑Hochberg correction across ~3 600 lag‑tests.

The null distribution is generated by permuting blocks of size b = 100 while preserving intra‑block order. This block‑permutation does not fully randomize the sign pattern and may retain residual autocorrelation structure, biasing the null distribution and inflating type‑I error rates.

concerns.text: Using only 1 000 permutations yields a minimum p‑value resolution of 0.001. Combined with Benjamini‑Hochberg correction over thousands of lag‑tests, the procedure may be overly conservative, further reducing the ability to identify genuine signals.
